html:
The Djeoromitxí, also called Jabutí, are a small Indigenous people of Rondônia in western Brazil, from the headwaters of the Rio Branco, a branch of the Guaporé. Their language, with Arikapú, forms the small Jabutian family, and about fifty people speak it.

Rubber tappers of the rubber boom moved many of them from their land in the 1900s. Today most live in the Rio Guaporé and Rio Branco reserves alongside the Makurap, Arikapú and Aikanã.
